newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian stocks at 3-year lows, further falls seen.
newsitem.headline: Indian stocks at 3-year lows, further falls seen.

text.p: Battered Indian stock markets are likely to pick up more bruises after testing three-year lows as companies reel under slowing demand and higher costs, brokers and analysts said on Wednesday.
"The trend is irreversibly down," said Ramesh Damani, a member-broker at the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE). "The clouds of recession are hanging over the market."

On Wednesday the index of the BSE, the country's premier bourse, was trading at 2,727.80 points at mid-session, down 70.20 points, or 2.51 percent, after reaching a three-year low on Tuesday and brokers predict more losses.
"I expect to see (the index at) 2,500 in four to six weeks," Damani said. "There's so much pessimism ... people are taking a fatalistic view."
Stock analysts said the tumble was triggered by stunning reverses in company performances for the first six months of fiscal 1996/97 (April-March).
Associated Cement Companies (ACC), India's largest cement firm, said last week its first-half net profit fell 56 percent to 550.50 million rupees ($15.4 million) from 1.25 billion rupees a year ago.
The market had expected a six-month profit of 800-900 million rupees. The company blamed increased fuel, freight and energy costs for the lower profits.

Profits were also hit at Century Textiles and Industries, aluminium maker Hindalco Industries, diversified firm Grasim Industries, Tata Power, Bombay Dyeing and steel manufacturer Steel Authority of India.
Analysts said scarce bank funds, high interest rates and slower sales growth were other factors that had squeezed profits.
"We're heading for a recession -- not a slowdown," said Ulhas Paymaster, another BSE broker. "The second-half results will be worse."
He said foreign funds, which had been the only major buyers this year, had started to sell because analysts had lowered their profit expectations.
"If the (selling) momentum picks up the (BSE) index will sink to 1,900-2,000," Paymaster said. "Even if the foreigners hold on the index will hit 2,500 by mid-February."
He said it was impossible to expect confidence-wrecked retail investors and cash-starved domestic funds to support the market in the near term.
